memory_candidates.content: When a shared, concurrently-written file (e.g. index-entries.json, state.json) already carries pre-existing foreign uncommitted hunks unrelated to your own edit, do not pass it to git-commit-scoped.sh/git-commit-phase.sh -- both wholesale `git add` a named pathspec, sweeping foreign hunks into your commit. Instead: extract only your own hunk from `git diff` (locate it via its `@@` header), apply it to the index alone with `git apply --cached <patch>`, then commit with a bare `git commit -m ...` (no pathspec) alongside any other fully-clean files added normally via `git add`. This leaves the foreign hunks untouched and unstaged for their owning task.

git-commit-phase.sh's Containment Self-Check mechanically drops any files_touched path not in the task's own declared file_scope and deposits it into .return-meta.json's proposed_file_scope array. This proposal can be resolved directly within the same dispatch (not just left as a follow-up) by folding the proposed path into the task's own file_scope the next time that task's file_scope is itself being edited -- e.g. during a dedicated file_scope-correction phase.
